Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Welcome to JP Morgan Chase's fourth quarter of 2025 earnings call.
This call is being recorded. Your line will be muted for the duration of the call. We will now go live to the presentation.
The presentation is available on JP Morgan Chase's website. Please refer to the disclaimer in the back concerning forward-looking statements. Please stand by.
At this time, I would now like to turn the call over to JP Morgan Chase's Chairman and CEO, Jamie Dimon, and Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Barnum.
Mr. Barnum, please go ahead.
Thank you and good morning, everyone. This quarter, the firm reported net income of $13 billion, and EPS of $4.63, within ROTCE of 18%.
The results included the previously announced reserve bill of $2.2 billion in CCB related to the forward purchase commitment of the Apple Card portfolio.
Revenue of $46.8 billion was up 7% year on year on higher markets revenue, as well as higher asset management fees and auto lease income.
The increase in NIIX markets was primarily driven by higher-formwide deposit balances and revolving bonuses in card, largely offset by the impact of lower rates.

Expenses of $24 billion were up 5% year on year, predominantly driven by higher volume and revenue related expenses, and compensation growth, including from office hiring, partially offset by the release of an FDSD special assessment accrual.
Turning to the failure results reminds you that there were a few significant items in 2025, which are listed in the footnote.
Excluding those items, the firm reported full year net income of $57.5 billion, EPS of $20.18 revenue of $185 billion, within ROTCE of 20%.

In terms of the balance sheet, we ended the quarter with a standardized CG1 ratio of 14.5%, down 30 basis points versus the prior quarter, as net income was more than offset by capital distributions and higher RWA.

In this quarter's higher standardized RWA is driven by increases in lending across both full sale and retail, including the Apple card purchase agreement, which contributed about $23 billion of standardized RWA, partially offset by lower market risk RWA.

You'll see that sequentially, the advanced RWA is more significantly than standardized, and as you know, our SCB is now at the 2.5% floor, which makes advanced RWA more relevant, so we have added it to the page.
The Apple card transactions advanced RWA contribution was about $110 billion, based on the sum of expected drawn balances and undrawn lines on closing.
The elevated level of advanced RWA is temporary and is expected to reduce to approximately $30 billion in the near term.
Within core businesses, PCP reported net income of $3.6 billion or $5.3 billion, excluding the reserve bill for the Apple card portfolio.
The revenue of $19.4 billion was up 6% year on year, commonly driven by higher NII, on higher revolving balances and card, and a higher deposit margin in banking and wealth management.
A few points to highlight.
Consumers and small businesses remain resilient.

We continue to monitor leading indicators for any signs of stress, and despite weak consumer sentiment, trends in our data are largely consistent with historical norms, and we are not currently seeing the duration.
Across income groups, debit and credit sales volume continue to perform well up 7% year on year.

For the full year, we had strong growth in our franchise, with 1.7 million net new checking accounts, 10.4 million new card accounts, and record households and wealth management across digital and advised channels.
Next, the CIV reported net income of $7.3 billion.
Revenue of $19.4 billion was up 10% year on year, driven by higher revenues and markets, payments and security services.
Even with more color, IVPs were down 5% year on year, reflecting a strong prior year compare, and the timing of some deals they were pushed to 26.
In terms of the outlook, we expect strong line engagement and deal activity in 2026, supported by constructive market dynamics, which is reflected in our pipeline.
